conventions.convention: The spatial torus is (R/2πZ)^3 with Borel probability measure (2π)^−3 dx on a fundamental cube; Fourier characters are exp(ik·x), and H^s uses the sum of squared L² norms of weak derivatives through integer order s.

Periodic coefficient matrices A^μ are smooth and symmetric; A^0 is positive definite on the open admissible state set. The local analytic theory uses integer s≥5, compact state ranges, and Countable Choice.
P_N retains the Euclidean Fourier ball |k|≤N, with conjugate-symmetric coefficients for real-valued fields.
K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y) for the future unit normal; lowered curvature slots are R_abcd=g(R(e_c,e_d)e_b,e_a). The momentum constraint is div_h K−d tr_h K=κT(n,·)=−κj.

The dust reduction uses γ=−g with signature (+---), U=u normalized by γ(U,U)=1, r=ρc², e_0=U=∂_s, and Γ_0=0. The connection is tentative and metric-compatible until residual vanishing establishes torsion freedom.
Dust volume orientation has ε_0123=1; antisymmetrization brackets have weight 1/2; the reduction Schouten tensor is Ric−S_γγ/6, and the magnetic Weyl tensor uses the right dual.
The harmonic vector is H^a=g^bc(Γ^a_bc−barΓ^a_bc); the reduced equation subtracts ∇_(a H_b), and the Einstein residual is G+Λg−κT.
Strict fluid evolution requires ε+p>0 and 0<p′<1; c_s=√p′ is dimensionless. Geodesic dust permits nonnegative density only with velocity prescribed and geodesic also on zero-density regions.

Physical conclusions adopt the direct Einstein field law with κ=8πG_N/c⁴. Normalized u has g(u,u)=−1; SI four-velocity is cu, and dust energy density is mass density times c². No empirical inputs or empirical validation claims enter.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, for s≥5, a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on O, compact K⊂int K′⊂O, and every R≥0, there are T>0 and C such that every H^s datum taking values in K with norm at most R has a classical Sobolev solution on (−T,T), taking values in K′, with the stated uniform H^s and H^{s−1} time-derivative bounds.

Under Countable Choice, smooth coefficients on an open state set have the stated composition, difference, homogeneous commutator and multiplier estimates on bounded H^s data with compact value ranges and compact coefficient time intervals, for s≥5; clause (e) supplies high-order estimates controlled by the preceding Sobolev norm.

Under its compact time/value and uniform H^s hypotheses, a locally uniform H^{s−1} limit of the stated Galerkin solutions lies in L∞H^s, has distributional time derivative in L∞H^{s−1}, and is a classical C¹ solution with initial value u_0.

Assuming Countable and Dependent Choice, a fixed covariant matter model satisfying the three explicit reduction, complete-initialization/recovery and reduced-stress-conservation hypotheses has a smooth local development from complete smooth constrained data, on a variable-width neighborhood in R×Σ, with an intrinsic globally hyperbolic Cauchy neighborhood and complete-data geometric uniqueness.

Under Countable and Dependent Choice and the precisely stated smooth reduced dust equations, the residuals satisfy the constructed closed linear homogeneous symmetric hyperbolic system. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on D⁺_Ω(Σ)∪D⁻_Ω(Σ), recovering the Levi–Civita connection, prescribed curvature and full Einstein-dust equation without division by density.

Assuming Countable Choice, a smooth reduced solution with conserved stress, H=0 initially and vanishing initial normal Einstein residuals has H=E=0 on an open neighborhood of the entire spacelike initial surface.

Assuming Countable and Dependent Choice, the four specified branches—vacuum with Λ, fixed scalar model, strict barotropic fluid, and nonnegative geodesic dust with prescribed velocity—admit smooth local developments from their complete smooth constrained data, with the stated causal neighborhood and data-fixing future-isometry uniqueness.

concerns.concern: Definition (b), lines 57–63, defines torus functions as compositions 'u∘q' with u:R³→R^N, whereas (a) defines q:R³→T³. This composition is not typed: u cannot be evaluated at q(x). Both the C∞ test class and C^m class need the descended function on T³ whose pullback along q is the periodic Euclidean function. As written, the foundational test-function definition is undefined.

The Statement, lines 42–44, assumes only that h_0 is a 'smooth metric on this product neighborhood' with tangential restriction h and ∂_s h_0=0, then sets bar g=−ds²+h_0. These hypotheses do not require h_0 to have zero time and mixed slots. For Minkowski initial data h=Σ(dx^i)², K=0, choose h_0=f(x¹)ds²+h with f=1/2+(1/4)tanh(x¹). This is a smooth time-independent Riemannian metric with the required restriction, and bar g is Lorentzian. But barΓ¹_00=−f′/2, while the prescribed g_0 jet has Γ=0, so H¹=−f′/2≠0. Thus conclusion (b) and Fact L3 fail under the literal hypotheses. The intended lifted spatial metric must be specified explicitly.

Proof 2.1 says the four Hamiltonian/momentum constraints are 'exactly Ric^γ_00=J_00 and Ric^γ_0a=J_0a' before constructing the remaining R^γ_0a0b components. The normal constraint fixes G^γ_00, not Ric^γ_00; the latter depends on those remaining components. The mixed identification is valid. After imposing Ric^γ_ab=J_ab, the normal Einstein constraint can establish Ric^γ_00=J_00 by a further trace calculation, but the claimed equivalence at the preceding stage is false.

The introductory conventions call U 'the unit future timelike vector U=n', although the prerequisite defines U=u and supplies no n here. A hypersurface normal would generally differ from U in the permitted tilted branch. Remove or define this unexplained equality so the observer is unambiguous.

Proof 4.1 ends its Gaussian-chart paragraph with justification tags, then continues the same cone-energy argument in an unnumbered paragraph beginning 'In this chart', with another tag group. This does not satisfy the requested one-complete-step-per-paragraph layout. No formatter or validation gate was run in this read-only dispatch.

alerts.finding: Definition (e) gives H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)\I⁻(D⁺(S)), then describes it as points 'not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. Membership in I⁻(D⁺(S)) means being chronologically before some point of D⁺(S). The displayed formula excludes points chronologically followed by a point of D⁺(S); the explanatory sentence reverses this direction.

Definition (b) calls the displayed T^{ab}=ρu^au^b a 'smooth symmetric covariant 2-tensor field'. Those upper-index components represent the contravariant tensor. The following equivalent T_ab formula correctly supplies its covariant version. The tensor-type wording should distinguish the two.
